txt: (Sings.) "Our bar, our bar, Hardie bar!"
He looks off to the side, eyes filled with worry. "I haven't *got* shit, Al."
He scoffs.
Him neither. Mostly keeps to his tomato juice, or whatever he's got there.
In the far back, Eugene is doing his best to ignore you...
In the far corner: standard working boot, steel reinforced toes, size 44. Forty-something, non-alcoholic beverage in hand. (You squint.) Is that a *plectrum*?
On his neck. Forget it. It's not important.
The man is silent.
"'Show me your cunt! Why don't you show me your cunt?' Then he gets knocked on the head with a wine bottle -- doesn't even fall down!" He shakes his head in disbelief.
"*I* think you're losing it, fiddle-man."
"*If* it's true." He looks at Shanky, then Titus. "But it's not -- right?"
"...both of you," he turns to the lieutenant. "We shouldn't have fucked with you like we did. You got between us and a lot of bullets in that fight. Martinaise owes you one."
"A live grenade." The man spreads his arms. "Right here in *our* bar!"
"Alain? He won't be leading anything." He turns to his friend. "I mean, look at him -- the man's broken through and through."
"Anyone ever tell you you're a total dickhead?" His voice is quiet and resigned. "Well... you are, man. Just fuck off and leave us be."
"Areopagite?" He starts laughing. "Boss, I think he's trying to say me and Theo."
"Boss, I think he's just gonna keep saying cock carousel."
"Brutal, Titus." He shakes his head. "Brutal but true. She has a hold on him."
"But he's got his window fitting business, a wife with two kids and the third one on the way... No way he's gonna leave all that."
"Carly said they've been trying to set up a *race rally*, whatever the fuck that means. Trying to get the *kipts* out of Revachol, before the economy goes to shit..."
"Carly said they've been trying to set up a mass execution." He shakes his head in disdain. "Bulk-purchasing guns. Ammunition, too."
"Cause one night he walked straight up to the mic and said: 'I'm Oranjese goddamn Special Forces and I'm gonna fuck you all'."
"Cop, you just don't understand how things work." He exhales sharply in frustration, but then quickly collects himself.
"Couldn't help you even if I wanted to." He shakes his head. "The whole harbour is in lockdown and Evrart sent word to sit tight and wait for instructions."
"Cunn and what-the-fuck now?" He stares at Cuno, scratching his head.
"Damn songbird of misery that one..." The man shakes his head.
"Did he just call you a *pussy-boy*?"
"Didn't Monica have giant titties?"
"Does he look like he's okay?"
"Easy, Al." The man says soothingly. "Don't let him get to you. Have one for Auntie LePlante, huh?"
"Fuck this..." The man starts pulling something out from his pocket.
"Fuck, Dennis, we don't kill you if you work for the company! Half the harbour works for the company..."
"Goddamn Shanky... never liked that rat-faced fuck."
"Goddamnit, we need to close that dump down for good."
"Hardie boys are local legends now."
"He wasn't, that's the thing." He sighs heavily. "Titus, Theo, Dennis, Angie... they're all gone, but he got away without a scratch."
"Hell, you both look like you could use some feminine company right now."
"Hey," Eugene interjects. "Wasn't Evrart's B Team looking for her the other day? They said something about her... I dunno, finding something?"
"I ain't gonna stick around for that." He shakes his head resolutely. "I only stayed because of Titus. *There* was a man born to lead."
"I don't do karaoke, man. I'm too good."
"I like that." The young guy nods. "Been thinkin' the same thing myself."
"I suppose," he continues, his voice now calm, "I should at least consider sticking around. If I'm not here, it's all over."
"I will. You take care of yours," he nods to you.
"I wouldn't go that far -- but you have a home here if you need it. And two busted up Union men who are grateful to you. So take care, okay?"
"I wrote a song about the fight, anybody wanna hear it, or...? Too soon, I get it."
"I'm on it, boss. Right when the law clears, me and Angus are going up there."
"I've seen the winch."
"If that's the case then it's not right." He looks at Titus, then Alain. "But it's not the case -- right?"
"If you think this will keep him from offin' himself, I'll make sure to remind him... so far I've just been pouring whiskey in him to keep him sedated." He nods.
"It wasn't for your fucking entertainment, Dennis. She..." He gets a hold of himself.
"It's just two doors," he agrees "We're not giving you *Ruby* for that -- she's practically a Hardie."
"It's just two doors," he cuts in. "We're not giving him *Ruby* for that -- she's one of *us*."
"It's just two doors. We're not giving you *Ruby* for that -- she's one of *us*."
"It's never a Sam Bo fighter and it's never a bullet-bending sniper."
"It's not *bewildering*, it's, like -- whatever, man." He looks around. "Guys, I'm not the only one who knew right?"
"Let's not get ahead of ourselves." He frowns. "We'll see what he does with the whole Shanky business."
"Liberal, man? Ruby's like a hard core patriot. You'd have to be blind not to..." He looks around. "Guys, I'm not the only one who *knew*, right?"
"Like hell it is! I still can't believe he called you a *pussy-boy*, Titus. What does that mean?"
"Look, what do you want from us, man? Things are pretty tough right now."
"Man, I've been to Jamrock. The place looks like a modern painting. Kids as old as ten with guns on the street -- you got eight different mobs vying for power..."
"Man, getting shot has really squeezed all the *funk* out of you." The guy looks up from his table. "Mark my words, one day we'll look back to this day and remember their courage, not their deaths."
"Man, now he's just throwing shit against the wall to see what sticks."
"Man... you have no idea how this works do you?" He looks at the glass of milk on the table. "But yes... If I don't stick around then it's all over. So I guess I sorta have to now."
"Me? No, man... I'm not a leader." He smiles suddenly. "You know Titus only recruited me 'cause I play the guitar? Said the team could use the morale boost."
"Nah. Garte said she took off some time before the firefight, that's all. Trying to remember if there was anything... oh, yeah, he said she seemed to be in real hurry."
"Never even seen it. Someone must have hidden it there before this room became our place."
"Never thought I'd miss the smell of Angie's rotting feet..."
"No shit, Mullen."
"No, man," Eugene raises his hand. "Pin it on me and frame me good, mister Law!"
"No, man. I don't know... I guess the Union will still be policing the neighbourhood, but..." He looks at his dazed companion. "Who's gonna do it now?"
"No, they totally said what it was... What was it..." He's still thinking it over in the corner. "Anyone remember?"
"Oh, he's itching for one..." He clacks his tongue. "I listen to Channel 8. This cop has a death wish."
"Oh, it's you... Didn't think we'd see you walking any time soon." He looks to the man behind him. "Alain, look, it's the rat cop."
"Oh, it's you... Didn't think we'd see you walking any time soon." He looks to the man sitting behind him. "Alain, look, it's the cowardly cop."
"Oh, it's you... Didn't think we'd see you walking any time soon." He looks to the man sitting behind him. "Alain, look, it's the killer cop."
"Oh, they're itching for one..." He clacks his tongue. "I listen to Channel 8. These cops have a death wish."
"One day I'll write a song about it."
"Or Denisse, the diner girl! The milk rack on that one..." He says, almost elegiacally.
"Or go pay your partner a visit in the hospital. I hear he got shot up pretty bad."
"Or you might die of a heart failure... Or syphilis?"
"Plus, man, it's like *female intuition* you know. Women talk to women." He peeks at Titus. "Which is sorta why we need someone on the team who they talk to."
"Really, Shanks? Klaasje wanted to talk to another girl, that's all. She was just the first one up there; *I* could've come up with that plan, if I'd been first."
"Relax, Dennis, no one is fucking you yet," says the forty-something man from the corner, with a plectrum hanging from his neck.
"Right." The man sips on his milk.
"She didn't fuck you 'cause you're *forty* and you still live with your mom, Dennis." Light laughter sounds off in the room. It feels nervous.
"She's not a ghost, she's gay. You'd have to be an idiot not to..." He looks around. "Guys, I'm not the only one who knew, right?"
"Shit like that can turn a man into pacifist... Not me, but someone..."
"Shit like that really makes you think."
"Shit, boss, he actually *is* racist!"
"Shut the fuck up, Shanky."
"So which one was it, man?"
"So...?" The man shrugs and looks at you.
"Sounds like you're on some kind of carousel yourself. And it's not a pretty one."
"Strange... I even miss Angie's loud stomach..."
"Sure enough!" Eugene raises his glass in toast. "We're the *real* heroes on these streets!"
"Sure there is. Carly said they're bulk-purchasing confetti. Ribbons, too, and loudspeakers..." He shakes his head. "And *fireworks*! Carly works at a carnival shop, you see."
"T, let's fucking *do* it," the man presses through his teeth -- his hand is on his belt.
"Thanks for getting involved, man. Not a lot of cops would step in that line of fire, but you did."
"That *is* a nice way of putting it -- he stole it from a song, by this old guy who also got fucked by a woman. I can't remember his name, I think he's dead now."
"That shit ain't helping anyone, asshole. The fuck do you want with us anyway?"
"That wouldn't be funny even if we weren't surrounded by the ghosts of our fallen friends."
"The fuck is he saying?"
"They didn't see shit, man," he turns to you. "Kids getting shot, we had three shootings a week, fuckin' graffito everywhere -- you cops haven't shown up since the Thirties."
"They don't know, man -- they weren't here." He turns to you. "We had three shootings a week, kids dead, fuckin' *graffito* everywhere -- you cops haven't shown up since the Thirties."
"They don't know, man. They weren't here." He turns to you. "We had three shootings a week, kids dead, fuckin' graffito everywhere... You cops haven't shown up since the Thirties."
"Think Mañana could make a good Hardie boy?"
"Those numbers were an *ass-pull*, man."
"Tiberius? He doesn't wanna get mixed up in our shit. Titus has been buttering him for years on the count of all this being *fun as fuck*."
"Titus was..." His eyes meet yours. "But thanks for the vote of confidence. If I don't stick around, it's all over. So I guess sorta I have to now."
"We need some *real* music in here."
"We shouldn't have fucked with you like we did. You got between us and a lot of bullets in that fight -- Martinaise owes you one."
"We're not bees, we're men. We're socialists!"
"What about Mañana? Think he'd make a good Hardie boy?"
"What's gonna happen to the Hardie boys? Look around you, man. This shit is done. There are no more Hardie boys!"
"What? Fuck no! *If* I'd stay we'd keep the name to honour Titus."
"Whatever you've seen is peanuts. Look at the big picture, man. The place is a paradise -- and all thanks to Hardie boys!"
"Wish I had my guitar..."
"Word on the street is: 'Outgunned, the Hardie boys kill twenty Krenel mercs...'"
"Wouldn't wanna beat up his grandma." There's snickering in the room. Some of the men put their beers down.
"Wow, man, can we? I mean..."
"Yeah -- exactly. Why not, man?"
"Yeah -- no. Ruby's got more balls than a ball pit. You'd have to be an idiot not to..." He looks around. "Guys, I'm not the only one who knew, right?"
"Yeah -- really. Had a gin and tonic up there, sang some Oranjese paratrooper song, and said he's gonna fuck everyone."
"Yeah, Carly said you've been hanging around the adult diaper shop. Browsing the aisles, too ashamed to ask for assistance."
"Yeah, Carly said you've been hanging around the day-care centre. In the bushes, man. By the jungle-gym. Tryna' set up some weird field trip to your station, that's in your home..."
"Yeah, aren't you listening? It's done. Finito!"
"Yeah, everyone knows Glen loves guns."
"Yeah, he said it was his 'favourite joint' now, started coming here every night! Drinking, grabbing girls -- grabbed one of ours mid-karaoke. Right there on the stage!"
"Yeah, like that changes anything."
"Yeah, man, weren't you listening?"
"Yeah, man, you're like a radio genius or something. Those notes are some in depth stuff. Indexes and shit."
"Yeah, man. *Theoretically* that's what you would do -- to get rid of the gangs, the dealers, even some of the junkies."
"Yeah, that's what the labour movement is *all* about. Clean and organized. And the Hardie boys are runnin' it."
"Yeah, there's always gonna be little sprouts. People find a way to make coin. But that's the little picture... Hardie boys are taking care of the big picture!"
"Yeah, this girl's on the mic, a beautiful girl, young. Gets into the second verse of 'Lover Lake'. The fucker grabs her legs, starts screaming..."
"Yeah, we're all very focused. What does it mean?"
"Yeah, what's up with that?"
"Yeah, with us, drinking. Near the stage there." He points to the karaoke stage.
"Yeah, you too. It's a rough world out there..." He shakes his head. "It's not easy being a cop. We were too hard on you..."
"Yeah..." The man seems unsure of himself.
"You doing a hell of a job, man! Hell of a job!"
"You got it boss! Professional law enforcement will investigate."
